g.text: tinyPLC A1 / TECHNICAL ASSEMBLY / 1 of 2
A1 printing, assembly and first build
Use the A1 visual guide with the design decisions and matching A1 BOM/CAD. A1 now has a routed
controller board that passes the configured CAD checks. Printing and card fit checks can start
now. Review the routing decisions, resolve remaining purchasing choices and inspect
fabrication outputs before ordering.
1. Print the 54 × 32 × 2.4 mm fit coupon first. Try the actual power switch in its 12.90 ×
19.81 mm opening; try M3 and M2 taps in the 2.5 and 1.6 mm pilots, and the 3 mm light rod
in the 3.2 mm bore. Reject cracking, loose retention or binding. Measure the drawings' 100
mm scale bar before using paper templates. 2. Print the white base floor-down and the white
lid outside-face-down using the supplied print STLs in mm. The lid's tall columns and
optical sleeves face upward. Start with a 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layers and multiple
perimeters; review bridge/support paths and record the real profile. Sand or paint only
external cosmetic surfaces; preserve mating faces and optical bores. 3. Deburr and test the
empty lid. Tap the four PCB pilots and four lid-column pilots M3; tap the four OLED post
pilots M2 after successful coupon trials. Cut a card controller template from drawing 03
and check mounting/port alignment. 4. With all supplies removed, snap SW3 into the left-side
aperture. Identify terminals 1 and 1A by the actual switch marking and continuity test, and
confirm the I position closes them. Prepare two insulated leads with proper 4.75 × 0.8 mm
female quick-connects and a suitable crimp tool. The connection boots and wire bending room
require a physical trial. 5. After PCB review and electrical bring-up, lower the board onto
the posts, DI row toward the four front openings. Inspect underside leads. Secure with four
M3 × 6 screws and nominal 0.5 mm M3 washers. Tighten gently in opposite corners; confirm no
bowing, bottoming or contact with the floor. 6. Connect J17.1 to SW3.1 and SW3.1A to J17.2.
Both are positive supply paths; never connect either to GND. Check OFF opens the loop and
ON closes it. Route the pair away from optical sleeves, the display and lid columns. 7.
Install two clear 3 mm rods, 24.6 mm long, through the lens pocket into their sleeves.
Their lower ends rest on the internal ledges. Check they stay above the LED packages and do
not press on them. Trial-fit the clear lens and its reverse black mask; align both clear
LED spots and the screen window. Bond only the lens perimeter using the nominal 0.2 mm
adhesive allowance. 8. With the lid upside down, place the Adafruit 326 QT module on its four
underside posts, glass facing the viewing aperture. Use four M2 × 6 screws and nominal 0.5
mm washers, from the rear of the module. Do not clamp glass or flex cable. Compare the
received board with the drawing and inspect the narrow post-to-glass clearance before
tightening. 9. Make the display harness: J16.1 → VIN/red, J16.2 → GND/black, J16.3 →
SCL/yellow, J16.4 → SDA/blue. The connector orders differ. Verify every wire by continuity,
leave a short service loop and unplug before removing the lid. Measure 3.3 V at the cable
before plugging in DS1. 10. Inspect for loose screws, cut leads and trapped wires. Check the
switch wire boots and display cable clear the lens sleeves and columns. Seat the lid
flush by hand, turn the unpowered enclosure over and install four M3 × 10 screws into the
underside counterbores. Tighten diagonally. Do not use screws to pull a warped lid into
place. Add four nominal 8 × 2 mm feet away from the screw heads so later service does not
destroy the feet. 11. Apply the labels from the A1 label sheet. Confirm J1.1 is +24 V, J1.2 is
0 V/GND (−); there is no PE terminal. Input contacts are DI/GND; output contacts are
protected +24 V/Q sink, not supply input pairs. All lettering in the render is a separate
applied label, not embossed STL geometry. 12. Record fit, screw engagement, cable paths, lens
visibility and any changes. Only after staged board bring-up and A1 firmware integration
should you test with the case closed. Measure temperature, power behavior and physical
outputs, including boot, OFF/ON and reset. The displayed RUN state must reflect actual
accepted scans. A working power light alone is not a PLC test.
Routed prototype; physical testing pending. Use matching A1 design, schematic, BOM and illustrated assembly guide.
